candidates.source_name: CBCG — Registar platnih institucija i njihovih agenata (Register of payment institutions and their agents)
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative, legally mandated actor list for the entire Montenegrin non-bank payments employer universe. Fetched content named 7 licensed PIs: MONTENEGRO TRANSFERS DOO, CAPITAL TRANSFER MNE DOO, MONETA MNE DOO, PAYSPOT ME DOO, ALTA PAY GROUP DOO, PRESTOPAY DOO, and Business Integration and Business Intelligence d.o.o. (all Podgorica). Each entry links a per-institution PDF that carries legal name, address and licensed service scope — the seed set from which all hiring/leadership tracking in this cell derives. Agent sub-registers also reveal distribution-network expansion, a leading indicator of field-staff hiring.
candidates.legal_status: official public register, published by the central bank
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled HTML scrape of the register page plus diffing of the linked per-institution PDFs (reg_montenegrotransfers.pdf, reg_capitaltransfer.pdf, reg_moneta.pdf, reg_payspot_me.pdf, reg_alta_pay_group.pdf, reg_prestopay.pdf, reg_busin_integr_and_busin_intell.pdf) under https://www.cbcg.me/slike_i_fajlovi/...; snapshot monthly and alert on added/removed entities or agents.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search for the regulator's register, then direct fetch and snowball into entity list
queries_used: CBCG registar platnih institucija Crna Gora

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Registar institucija za elektronski novac i njihovih agenata (E-money institutions register)
candidates.why_relevant: The definitive EMI actor list. On fetch it stated the register currently contains no entered e-money institution ('U Registru trenutno nema upisane institucije za elektronski novac'). That is itself high-value intelligence: the EMI segment in Montenegro is empty, so any first entry is a market-entry event that will be immediately followed by country-manager/compliance-officer hiring. Worth monitoring precisely because it is a zero-state that will change.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly change-detection on the page body; trigger a high-priority alert the moment the empty-register sentence disappears.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search + direct fetch
queries_used: institucija za elektronski novac Crna Gora registar CBCG

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Registar platnih sistema (Register of payment systems / system operators)
candidates.why_relevant: Identifies licensed payment-system operators in Montenegro — the infrastructure layer employers (clearing/settlement operators) distinct from PIs. The page publishes a 'Pregled registra' PDF; the HTML body itself carried no names in my fetch, so the operator list lives inside the PDF and must be pulled from there.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Locate and download the 'Pregled registra' PDF linked from the page, OCR/parse operator names, then diff on a quarterly cadence.
candidates.discovered_via_method: sibling-page snowball from the registri index
queries_used: CBCG registar platnih institucija Crna Gora

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Spisak platnih institucija i institucija za elektronski novac kojima je oduzeto odobrenje (revoked-licence list)
candidates.why_relevant: Licence withdrawal is the strongest possible org-change signal for a payments employer: it precedes or accompanies wind-down, mass departures and talent release into the market. Complements the positive registers by capturing exits, which registers of live entities silently drop.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly diff of the list; cross-reference removals from the live PI register against this list to classify exit vs. rename.
candidates.discovered_via_method: sibling-page snowball from CBCG registri index
queries_used: CBCG registar platnih institucija Crna Gora

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Pružaoci finansijskih usluga / kontrolna funkcija (supervised financial service providers hub)
candidates.why_relevant: Supervisory hub that aggregates the categories of supervised entities and typically routes to licensing decisions. CBCG approves 'fit and proper' persons for management bodies of payment institutions, so licensing/approval decisions published under the supervisory function are a primary route to named leadership appointments — the highest-value item for this cell's leadership-moves topic.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the kontrolna-funkcija subtree for decision/odluka pages mentioning 'saglasnost' or 'imenovanje' plus 'platna institucija'; parse named individuals.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search snowball
queries_used: institucija za elektronski novac Crna Gora registar CBCG

candidates.source_name: Bankar.me — Oglasi za posao (financial-sector job-ads category)
candidates.why_relevant: Single highest-yield hiring source found for this cell. Bankar.me is the Montenegrin banking/finance trade portal and it republishes payment-institution vacancies verbatim — a confirmed example is 'Platna institucija PaySpot ME doo Podgorica otvara više pozicija: Regionalni menadžer prodaje za regije Sjever, Jug i Centralnu regiju', which reveals both headcount growth and a three-region field-sales org structure. It also runs director-level ads ('Direktor sektora...', 'zapošljava Izvršnog direktora'), covering the leadership-moves topic.
candidates.legal_status: public trade media; observe robots.txt and rate limits
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Poll the category page (and any RSS feed) weekly; extract employer name, role title, region and deadline; filter for the CBCG PI actor list to isolate non-bank payments hiring.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language actor-name search that surfaced a trade-portal republication, then snowballed to the portal's job category

candidates.source_name: CRPS — Centralni registar privrednih subjekata (Montenegro companies register) and its search portal
candidates.why_relevant: The statutory source of truth behind every aggregator: legal form and status, founding date, names of legal representatives (zastupnici), founders and ownership structure, and registered activities. Changes to the registered representative are the legally definitive record of a leadership move at a Montenegrin PI, and land here before any press mention. Run by the Tax Administration; extracts can also be requested electronically.
candidates.access_status: open_public search; some extracts on request
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Query by each PI's legal name; snapshot the representative/founder block quarterly and diff. Note the portal is HTTP and may be session/form-driven, so a browser-driven fetch is likely needed rather than plain HTTP GET.

The processing layer appears to be served by regional vendors (Payten/Asseco SEE, which does have a Podgorica office) and by banks' in-house acquiring, rather than by a locally registered specialist.

brief: Montenegro's non-bank payments employer universe is small, fully enumerable and regulator-anchored: the CBCG payment-institution register names seven licensed PIs (Montenegro Transfers, Capital Transfer MNE, Moneta MNE, PaySpot ME, Alta Pay Group, PrestoPay, and Business Integration and Business Intelligence), all Podgorica-based, while the e-money institution register is currently empty and the payment-system operator list sits inside an unparsed PDF. Because these firms employ single-digit to low-double-digit headcounts, they publish almost no owned careers content; hiring signal instead concentrates in the trade portal bankar.me (which republishes PI vacancies verbatim, including PaySpot ME's three-region sales-manager expansion) and in the state employment agency ZZZCG, with commercial boards as recall backstops. Leadership and org change is best detected structurally rather than editorially — via CRPS legal-representative filings, CBCG fit-and-proper consents, and aggregator fields such as CompanyWall's director and employee-count data (which showed Alta Pay Group at roughly 8 staff under director Maja Armenko). The card acquiring/processing layer has no Montenegro-domiciled specialist and must be covered through regional vendor Payten/Asseco SEE's Podgorica operation and through the Serbian parent groups of several PIs, whose cross-border postings often signal Montenegrin build-outs first.
